program: Survivor legal advocacy, trauma counseling and family safety
priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: AVDA provides legal advocacy and trauma support for domestic-abuse survivors in Greater Houston and neighboring counties.
Its attorneys and advocates help with safety planning, protective orders, divorce, custody and access to practical resources.
The deep review assesses both health and net household resources, using a newer Harris County support reference and full client burdens.
strengths: Primary grant and service records identify a local legal-advocacy delivery route and concrete resource mechanisms.
Randomized intensive advocacy research supports possible lasting safety and wellbeing gains, while its transfer to AVDA remains a judgment.
The model keeps household costs and transfer-payer losses even when outcomes would also occur through alternatives.
reservations: Supported adults and children are not deduplicated households, completed cases or clinical responders.
The exact current recipient outcomes and donation-sensitive capacity remain unverified, and the latest reviewed cost is FY 2023.
Income research is observational; local utility, earnings, overlap and burden values remain conditional hypotheses.

sections.what: AVDA provides legal advocacy and trauma support for domestic-abuse survivors in Greater Houston and neighboring counties. Its attorneys and advocates help with safety planning, protective orders, divorce, custody and access to practical resources. The deep review assesses both health and net household resources, using a newer Harris County support reference and full client burdens.
sections.monitoring: A primary Impact100 Houston 2025 award entry describes more than 2,500 Harris County survivors supported in 2024 and a $24,666 legal-advocacy grant. We use 2,500 as a rounded lower descriptive reference, not an exact observed unique cohort or successful legal outcome. It includes women and children. Request distinct adult households, completed cases, counseling dose, time to safety, retained earnings and payer incidence. The official 2024 report is linked through Canva but its body was inaccessible; current homepage 2025 counters also lack retrievable numbers. Neither is treated as reviewed output. BIPP and outreach are not added to this cohort.
sections.qualitative: The 1994 randomized intensive postshelter advocacy study found better quality of life but no significant between-group physical-abuse difference at six months. The larger 1999 randomized study followed 278 women over two years and found less violence, better quality of life and improved resource access. Both used intensive ten-week advocacy, not AVDA’s measured legal/counseling dose; neither supplies a local QALY coefficient. The Iowa legal-aid panel followed 150 women initially, 85 at one year and 32 at two years; it found favorable changes but no relationship with type or amount of legal services and no untreated comparison. A later income paper reports about $5,500 total annual income change after private/public components, not causal disposable earnings or a charity-return estimate. The model therefore retains uncertain finite health and net-resource judgments and tests the observational figure separately. Houston legal services include Harris, Fort Bend, Austin, Waller, Grimes and Washington; the current numerator is Harris-only, so it uses local share 1 rather than attributing all regional activity to Houston.
sections.cost: Initial $3,105,274.58 becomes $13054938.99 per better life (ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents). The change comes from replacing the historical regionwide reference with a newer Harris-only support reference and correcting burdens to include all exposed households, not just additional outcomes. Whole FY 2023 cost remains $4,051,637; this partial local channel is not a measured whole-portfolio or marginal-gift return. Health is 4.230100 QALYs, signed income/consumption is -1.126572 welfare equivalents, and combined benefit is 3.103528. Income is assessed, not set to zero or omitted because it is negative. Judgments: 2,500 supported adults/children × 0.5 household mapping gives 1,250 exposed household proxies. Additional case response 0.3 gives 375 incremental outcome households; conditional clinical response 0.25 gives 93.75 responders. Utility 0.03 for two years, half-year delay and 3% discount are retained transfer judgments; clinical utility covers physical/trauma symptoms only, not the same financial security already in resources. All 1,250 households retain full 0.001 QALY harm and $100 incremental access burden, including clients whose outcomes alternative aid might produce. Of the 375 additional outcomes, resource response 0.3 gives 112.5 households with one-year net work resources $1,500, otherwise-paid medical costs $100 and external support resources $800. Positive-only overlap 0.5 leaves $1,100 after the separate full access cost; the remaining 1,137.5 households incur the full $100 burden. These are not observed success rates or causal dollar gains. The $1,500 is disposable after tax, withdrawn benefits and recurring work costs; access burden is a distinct cost, not deducted twice. Existing AVDA emergency cash is excluded as a new gain because it is already financed through the numerator. Full $800 counterpart losses per successful recipient are spread over a judged distinct 10,000 payer households at $35,000 baseline, with geographic share applied once. Payer distribution is uncertain, including whether the abuser and recipient remain one consumption unit. No property award, retail legal fee or ordinary survivor earnings is a new income gain. Negative components and full external/retaliation costs are not overlap-discounted. The $5,500 sensitivity is an unadjusted historical association, not a causal after-cost income prediction; overlap and explicit burdens still apply. Zero additional outcome retains harms/costs; no-exposure is tested separately. Shorter duration, clinical-null, financial-only, adverse, payer-loss and full-resource cases remain inspectable. At the unchanged historical regionwide cohort and local share, correcting all-exposed burdens alone gives $5,696,855.08, versus the initial $3,105,274.58; the remaining change to $13,054,938.99 is chiefly the narrower newer Harris reference. This is not evidence that AVDA’s whole portfolio became four times less effective: other counties, BIPP, prevention and child-specific effects remain unmeasured, not assumed zero.
sections.funding: Current expanded working-poor representation is free, while clients may contribute court costs and fees; AVDA validates legal clients’ parking, so the $100 burden is an uncertain combined court/travel/time increment rather than an asserted parking fee. Other legal aid, public protections, compensation programs, private counsel where affordable and family support form the alternative. The new grant shows support for legal advocacy, not measured extra completed cases or an unrestricted gift bottleneck. Nine current attorney/paralegal teams do not establish spare capacity. A newer FY 2024 audit is listed but its original body was not retrieved; its index flags a material weakness, not verified cost or fraud. Full opportunity costs and other portfolio outcomes remain unresolved.

model.costScope: Whole reviewed FY 2023 AVDA annual cost versus a conditional newer Harris-only survivor support channel; unmatched vintage and partial portfolio, not marginal gift EV.
model.geographicAttribution: Rounded 2024 Harris County support reference only; g=1 for this local cohort. Whole recipient cost also covers nonlocal and unmodeled programs.
model.formula: Exposed = N × unique. Incremental outcome households = exposed × b. Health = (clinicalN × unique × b × clinicalResponse × q × finite discounted duration − exposed × full union harm discounted at onset) × g. Resources = one signed household log for successful/other exposed households plus full distinct payer/provider incidence with geography once. Price = 10 × annual cost / positive combined health and resources.
model.counterfactual: Other legal aid, public protection and benefit systems, affordable private counsel where available, alternative counseling, family support and case outcomes without this provider.
model.attribution: b is the share of supported household proxies whose outcomes improve beyond alternative providers; clinicalResponse and resource success are distinct conditional outcomes, not marginal-gift probability. Harms and access costs cover all exposures irrespective of b.
model.uncertainty: Rounded supported survivor count is source-based; household mapping, causal response, utility, duration, resource gains, payer incidence and capacity remain judgments. Randomized external advocacy does not identify AVDA causal effects; observational income change does not identify attributable disposable earnings.
model.nativeOutcomes: Primary grant-maker describes over 2,500 adult/child Harris survivors supported in 2024; not unique households, completed cases or causal health/resources. BIPP, outreach, other counties and child-specific effects remain unmodeled, not zero-valued.
